The daily heating pattern causes weather to form. Imagine you are on the ground on the east bank near an inland lake, looking at an inland hill, which faces the prevailing westers, which usually means from about west southwesward.

In summer and at night and in cold conditions and with light to mid-speed wests to north-westly (west, northwest, northwest-by-norte and so) prevailing and strong enough for clouds to not obscure the surface of your target, then, as day turns into afternoon the land warbs faster than its atmosphere does and thus a land breeze blows in the afternoon, off from you toward, from east toward, to and onto or up to or over to or upon (your) east hillside.

The sun warmls (by the sun heating ground) land more on or over the west bank. And
